title: velvet-shift-notes-scratch
body:
Velvet shift - quick digest (late night scribbles)

Context: picking up from 23:00 -> 07:00. Quiet start; two small items to watch: intermittent 504s from hosted-api-us-west (gateway) and a latency blip on embedder-01 pool. Both are low frequency but correlated with spikes in short seq batching.

Open items at start:
- JIRA-OPS-3821: Intermittent 504s from hosted-api-us-west (owner: Diego). Happened 02:14, 02:47, 03:32. Gateway logs show upstream 502 then connection reset. No recent deploy.
- Temporary KV eviction experiment applied on ded-gpu-3 yesterday (note in Confluence link). Keep an eye on cache miss-rate for models with long context.

Immediate triage steps (if you see a 504):
1) Check gateway error rate dashboard: Console -> Routes -> hosted-api -> 5xx by upstream.
2) SSH to gateway-primary (gw-usw-2): sudo journalctl -u gateway -n 500 | grep "502\\|connection reset".
3) If upstream 502s present, run curl -v to model-router endpoint from gateway host: curl -sS -D - https://10.1.120.11:8443/ping -o /dev/null.
4) If ping fails, escalate to infra on-call (Diego) and open quick incident note in JIRA-OPS-3821 with timestamps and gateway logs snippet.

Helpful quick commands (copy/paste):
- tail gateway logs (last 1k lines): sudo journalctl -u gateway -n 1000 --no-pager
- check router pod restarts: kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=model-router -o wide
- scrape cache-metrics: curl -s http://ded-gpu-3:9100/metrics | grep kv_cache_miss_rate

Observed patterns while triaging:
- 504s often follow bursts of small requests (<= 32 tokens) that flood the short-seq batching pool. Looks like batching window saturates and backend times out.
- ded-gpu-3 eviction changes bumped miss-rate from ~2% -> ~9% for two models; downstream latency increased ~40ms median in the short window.

Temporary workaround taken by Diego (notes):
- Increased batching window for short-seq pool from 8ms -> 12ms on ded-gpu-3 (config id: shortseq-window-2026-03-10-01). This reduced 504s in the 02:00-03:00 window but caused slight latency uptick for single-token completions.

If issue resurfaces (playbook):
- Flip shortseq-window back to 8ms during morning low-load if customer-facing latency matters more than throughput. Document change in the ticket with before/after metrics.
- Add temporary route-level fallback: hosted-api route -> fallback to model-small-quant when router load > 80% for >2min. Use console rollout to apply canary 10% first.

Pending ops and reminders for next shift:
- Verify if the KV eviction experiment needs rollback (check ded-gpu-3 miss-rate and 99th p99 latencies over last 24h).
- Follow up with Applied ML: they were going to test quantized variant on dedicated pool to see perf/cost tradeoffs (PR #614 on GH).
- Draft short blurb for morning stand: "Observed transient 504s tied to short-seq batching; mitigated by increasing batching window; evaluating longer-term config vs quantized fallback."

Notes-to-self / gotchas:
- Don't restart model-router during active incident unless Diego confirms — causes brief SLO breach due to cold KV cache rebuild.
- If you must restart, do it one zone at a time and route traffic to fallback region (console -> routing -> override).
- When copying logs into JIRA, scrub IPs (use grep -v or sed) — privacy rule reminder.

Quick escalation contacts:
- Diego Alvarez (infra on-call) - pager -> +1-555-0102, slack @diego (primary)
- Riley Morgan (serving-runtime) - slack @riley.m (backup)
- SRE lead (Maya Chen) - pager only for sev2+

Questions / things to resolve:
- Are the short-seq batching windows globally consistent? I saw a mismatch between ded-gpu-3 and ded-gpu-5 configs. If mismatch is intentional, document the reason in infra runbook.
- Confirm if the quantized fallback has warmup steps to avoid cold-start token penalty. Applied ML to confirm.

End-of-shift checklist (for handing off):
- Add summary to JIRA-OPS-3821 with latest metrics and config change ids.
- Post short note in #sre-ops that "Velvet shift: increased shortseq window 8->12ms on ded-gpu-3; monitoring".
- Mention to morning standby: watch 02:00-04:00 window for recurrence.
- If no recurrence by 09:00, tag ticket as "monitoring:resolved-provisional".

Loose brainstorm (if time permits):
- Add a tiny local probe on gateway to detect bursty small-request patterns and preemptively trigger route-level throttling for guests to reduce queueing. (Prototype: gateway-probe -> simple histogram over 30s -> if >X small-req/s then set route weight shift to fallback).

Random scribbles / shorthand log: 
- 02:14 504 gw-usw-2 upstream 502 conn-reset -> rolled window 8->12 -> 02:27 drop in 504s
- 03:03 embedder-01 p99 +120ms -> correlate with kv_miss spike

If anything breaks while I'm asleep: flag to morning team and put on-call note under my name in the ticket.

-- Aisha K. (velvet shift)

"This is a working doc — leave quick notes rather than polished summaries. Save changes with timestamp in the edit comment."
